name: Tobadill
kurzbeschreibung: Tiny, authentic mountain village above Landeck, surrounded by endless forests and crisp, crystal-clear mountain air.
beschreibung:
Overview

Tobadill is situated at an elevation of 1,136 meters in the Tyrolean Oberland, resting on a sun-drenched plateau at the entrance of the Paznaun Valley high above the steep Trisanna Gorge. Just below this peaceful mountain village of roughly 515 residents, the Trisanna River from Paznaun and the Rosanna River from the Stanzertal merge to form the Sanna River. The settlement features a traditional dispersed layout consisting of picturesque hamlets such as Feld, Perfuchsberg, Plattils, and Badstube clinging gracefully to the slopes. To the southwest rise the formidable crests of the Verwall Alps, crowned by the Hoher Riffler at 3,168 meters, while the Lechtal Alps frame the horizon to the north. Far from busy thoroughfares, Tobadill preserves pristine pine woodlands, profound tranquility, and authentic alpine farming heritage.

History

The settlement was first documented in 1275 as 'Taueldilli', a Rhaeto-Romanic toponym signifying a small hay barn. Perched dramatically on a rocky spur overlooking the river confluence stands 13th-century Schloss Wiesberg castle. Once controlled by the Counts of Rottenburg and Tyrolean sovereign rulers, the fortress was the stage for fierce skirmishes during the Tyrolean Rebellion of 1809 when local marksmen repelled invading Napoleonic regiments. Right beside the castle, the world-famous Trisanna Bridge spans the chasm: erected between 1882 and 1884 during the reign of Emperor Franz Joseph I for the Arlberg Railway, this striking viaduct with its 120-meter span and 87-meter clearance was celebrated as a global engineering marvel and the widest railway arch of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. In the hamlet of Feld stands the Baroque Parish Church of Saint Magnus, built around 1735 by Kassian Grießer with fine ceiling frescoes created in 1793 by Johann Georg Witwer.

Getting There

By car, travel via the Inntal Autobahn A12 and Arlberg Expressway S16 to the Pians/Paznaun exit. From the Silvretta Road B188 near Schloss Wiesberg, the panoramic state road L250 ascends the hillside in winding curves to Tobadill. Rail passengers arrive at Landeck-Zams station, an international hub along the Arlberg Railway. From Landeck, regular VVT bus line 4 runs multiple times daily across Perfuchsberg directly to the village center.

Tips

The iconic vantage point framing Schloss Wiesberg castle against the soaring arches of the Trisanna Bridge is one of the most celebrated railway photo opportunities in Europe. Walkers will appreciate the leisurely Tobadill circular trail winding through hamlets like Plattils and Badstube, providing scenic rest areas and vistas into the valley. For ambitious mountaineers, the village offers trail access into the Verwall range and stages of the Starkenberger panoramic route. Furthermore, Tobadill is noted for small-batch farm distilleries, where visitors can sample authentic Tyrolean fruit brandies.
